name: Missouri
agency: Missouri State Highway Patrol, Water Patrol Division

rule.phaseIn: Born after Jan. 1, 1984 and before Jan. 1, 2006: card needed on the lakes of the state. From Jan. 1, 2027, anyone born on or after Jan. 1, 2006 needs it on all state waters.
rule.textEn: Anyone born after Jan. 1, 1984 needs a Missouri boating safety ID card to operate a vessel on the state's lakes; from Jan. 1, 2027, those born in 2006 or later need it on all state waters.
rule.textEs: Quien nació después del 1 de enero de 1984 necesita la tarjeta de identificación de seguridad náutica de Misuri para manejar una embarcación en los lagos del estado; desde el 1 de enero de 2027, los nacidos en 2006 o después la necesitarán en todas las aguas del estado.

exemptions: Holders of a USCG master, mate or operator license.
Private lakes or ponds that are not waters of the state.
Non-residents with a NASBLA-approved certificate from another state.
Active members of the U.S. Armed Forces, reserves or Missouri National Guard, and their spouses.
Anyone who already completed a NASBLA-approved course.

card.feeNote: The Water Patrol may charge a cost-based fee for the card and replacements (amount not set in the statute). A 7-day temporary card from rental or sales businesses costs $9.

nonResident: Non-residents with a NASBLA-approved certificate or license from their state are exempt.
rental: Rental and sales businesses can issue a one-time temporary card valid up to 7 days ($9) after an affidavit and a valid driver license.
